proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(r_{ja}=p_je_{ja}\) and \(r_0=p_{\min}e_{\min}\).  By
\(\mathrm{ass:consistency}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:randomization}\),
\[
 E_{P_n}(Y\mid X=j,A=a)=E_{P_n}\{Y(a)\mid X=j\}=\mu_{n,ja}.
\]
Thus every coordinate of \(\xi_n\) is centered.  The same two assumptions and
the definitions of \(p_j\) and \(e_{ja}\) show that the covariance of
\(n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\xi_n(O_{ni})\) is \(V_n\).

We first record the finite-dimensional normal estimate used below.  If
\(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) are i.i.d., \(E X_i=0\),
\(E(X_iX_i^\top)=I_d\), and \(\|X_i\|_2\le B\), then
\[
 d_{\mathrm{BL}}\!\left\{
  {\cal L}\!\left(n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^nX_i\right),N(0,I_d)
 \right\}
 \le {32d^{3/2}B^3\over\sqrt n}.                                      \tag{1}
\]
Here is a self-contained verification of the estimate.  For a function \(f\)
bounded by one and one-Lipschitz, Gaussian convolution followed by integration
along the Ornstein--Uhlenbeck semigroup gives the Stein solution
\[
 g_f(x)=-\int_0^\infty
 \left[E f\!\left(e^{-s}x+\sqrt{1-e^{-2s}}\,Z\right)-Ef(Z)\right]ds ,
 \qquad Z\sim N(0,I_d).
\]
Differentiate the Gaussian kernel under the integral, split the integral at
\(s=n^{-1}\), and use \(|f(x)-f(y)|\le\|x-y\|_2\).  Coordinatewise Gaussian
integration by parts gives
\[
 \sum_{r,s=1}^d
 \left|E\!\left[
 \partial_{rs}g_f(W_i+\theta X_i/\sqrt n)
 -\partial_{rs}g_f(W_i)\right]X_{ir}X_{is}\right|
 \le {32d^{3/2}\over\sqrt n}E\|X_i\|_2^3,                              \tag{2}
\]
uniformly in \(0\le\theta\le1\), where
\(W_i=n^{-1/2}\sum_{k\ne i}X_k\).  To see the constant directly, on
\(s\le n^{-1}\) use the Lipschitz bound before differentiating, which
contributes at most \(8d^{3/2}E\|X_i\|_2^3/\sqrt n\); on
\(s>n^{-1}\), the two differentiated Gaussian densities have first absolute
moments at most \(2\sqrt d\) and second absolute moments at most \(4d\),
which contributes at most \(24d^{3/2}E\|X_i\|_2^3/\sqrt n\).
Taylor's formula, independence of \(W_i\) and \(X_i\), and
\(E(X_iX_i^\top)=I_d\) cancel the first two terms in the Stein identity
\(Ef(W)-Ef(Z)=E\{\operatorname{tr}\nabla^2g_f(W)-W^\top\nabla g_f(W)\}\).
Summing the remainders in (2) proves (1).

Apply (1) to \(X_i=V_n^{-1/2}\xi_n(O_{ni})\).  Assumptions
\(\mathrm{ass:stratum\mbox{-}mass}\),
\(\mathrm{ass:overlap}\), and \(\mathrm{ass:bounded\mbox{-}outcomes}\)
give
\[
 \|\xi_n(O)\|_2\le
 B_\xi:={2B_Y\sqrt{K-1}\over p_{\min}e_{\min}}.
\]
Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:covariance\mbox{-}envelope}\) gives
\(\|V_n^{-1/2}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le v_{\min}^{-1/2}\).  Since a linear
map of operator norm at most \(v_{\max}^{1/2}\) changes the
bounded-Lipschitz constant by at most
\(\max(1,v_{\max}^{1/2})\), (1) yields
\[
 d_{\mathrm{BL}}\!\left\{
 {\cal L}\!\left(n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\xi_n(O_{ni})\right),N(0,V_n)
 \right\}
 \le {C_{\mathrm{lin}}\over\sqrt n},\qquad
 C_{\mathrm{lin}}
 =32d^{3/2}\max(1,\sqrt{v_{\max}})
 {B_\xi^3\over v_{\min}^{3/2}}.                                      \tag{3}
\]

It remains to verify that the ratio estimator has the asserted linearization.
For a cell \(g=(j,a)\), write
\[
 N_g=\sum_{i=1}^n{\bf1}\{X_{ni}=j,A_{ni}=a\},\qquad
 S_g=\sum_{i=1}^n{\bf1}\{X_{ni}=j,A_{ni}=a\}(Y_{ni}-\mu_{n,ja}).
\]
On \(N_g>0\), the difference between the normalized cell mean and its
linear term is
\[
 D_g:=\sqrt n(\widehat\mu_{n,ja}-\mu_{n,ja})
       -{S_g\over\sqrt n\,r_{ja}}
 ={S_g(nr_{ja}-N_g)\over\sqrt n\,N_gr_{ja}}.                           \tag{4}
\]
On \(N_g\ge nr_{ja}/2\), Cauchy--Schwarz, bounded outcomes, and the binomial
variance formula imply
\[
 E\{|D_g|{\bf1}(N_g\ge nr_{ja}/2)\}
 \le {2\{E S_g^2\,E(N_g-nr_{ja})^2\}^{1/2}
          \over n^{3/2}r_{ja}^2}
 \le {4B_Y\over\sqrt n\,r_0}.                                        \tag{5}
\]
The multiplicative Chernoff calculation
\[
 P(N_g<nr_{ja}/2)\le \exp(-nr_{ja}/8)\le\exp(-nr_0/8)                 \tag{6}
\]
also includes the empty-cell event.  On this exceptional event the convention
\(\widehat\mu_{n,ja}=0\) and \(|\mu_{n,ja}|\le B_Y\) give
\[
 |D_g|\le2B_Y\sqrt n(1+r_0^{-1}).
\]
Since \(n e^{-nr_0/8}\le8/(e r_0)\), (5)--(6) imply, for every \(n\),
\[
 E|D_g|\le {C_g\over\sqrt n},\qquad
 C_g={4B_Y\over r_0}
 +{16B_Y(1+r_0^{-1})\over e r_0}.                                    \tag{7}
\]
Each contrast remainder is \(D_{(j,a)}-D_{(j,0)}\).  Hence
\[
 E\left\|E_n-n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\xi_n(O_{ni})\right\|_2
 \le {2\sqrt d\,C_g\over\sqrt n}.                                    \tag{8}
\]
The coupling in (8), the Lipschitz part of the definition of
\(d_{\mathrm{BL}}\), and (3) prove the claim with the explicit choice
\[
 C_{\mathrm{BE}}
 =C_{\mathrm{lin}}+2\sqrt d\,C_g.
\]
This constant is a computable function of
\((J,K,p_{\min},e_{\min},B_Y,v_{\min},v_{\max})\), is independent of
the row law, and the argument is therefore uniform over the stated model
class.

Write \(q(v)=q_{c,b}(v)\) and \(\Psi(v)=\Psi_{c,b}(v)\).  Positivity of every
coordinate of \(b\), supplied by
\(\mathrm{ass:benchmark\mbox{-}support}\), makes every logarithm below finite.
Direct differentiation gives
\[
 \nabla\Psi(v)=q(v),\qquad \nabla^2\Psi(v)={1\over c}C\{q(v)\}.         \tag{9}
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \log{q(u+z)_a\over q(u)_a}
 ={z_a\over c}
 -\log{\sum_rb_r e^{(u_r+z_r)/c}\over\sum_rb_r e^{u_r/c}} .
\]
Multiplication by \(q(u+z)_a\), summation in \(a\), and multiplication by
\(c\) give
\[
 c\,\mathrm{KL}\{q(u+z)\|q(u)\}
 =z^\top q(u+z)-\Psi(u+z)+\Psi(u)
 =\ell_{c,b}(u,z).                                                     \tag{10}
\]
This proves nonnegativity as well.

For \(f(s)=\Psi(u+sz)\), two integrations of the fundamental theorem of
calculus yield
\[
 f(0)-f(1)+f'(1)=\int_0^1s f''(s)\,ds .
\]
Using (9) therefore gives
\[
 \ell_{c,b}(u,z)
 ={1\over c}\int_0^1s\,z^\top C\{q(u+sz)\}z\,ds.                       \tag{11}
\]
Convexity gives
\(\Psi(u+z)\ge\Psi(u)+z^\top q(u)\), whence
\[
 \ell_{c,b}(u,z)
 \le z^\top\{q(u+z)-q(u)\}\le\max_a z_a-\min_a z_a
 =\operatorname{osc}(z).                                              \tag{12}
\]
Finally, \(z^\top C(r)z=\operatorname{Var}_r(z_A)\), and the elementary
range inequality
\(\operatorname{Var}_r(z_A)\le\operatorname{osc}(z)^2/4\) follows by
centering at \((\max z+\min z)/2\).  Substitution in (11) gives
\[
 c\ell_{c,b}(u,z)
 \le\int_0^1s\,{\operatorname{osc}(z)^2\over4}\,ds
 ={\operatorname{osc}(z)^2\over8}.
\]
Together with (10), this proves all asserted inequalities.

Fix \(c>0\).  In stratum \(j\), the term involving the reference mean
\(\mu_{n,j0}\) is constant over lotteries.  Since
\(u_{n,j}=\sqrt n\,\Delta_{n,j}\) and
\(\lambda_n(c)=c/\sqrt n\), multiplication of the nonconstant part of
the welfare criterion by \(\sqrt n\) gives
\[
 (Ru_{n,j})^\top\pi_j-c\,\mathrm{KL}(\pi_j\|b_j).                      \tag{13}
\]
The Gibbs variational identity, obtained by substituting the definition of
\(q_{c,b}\), is
\[
 \sup_{\pi\in\Delta^{K-1}}
 \{v^\top\pi-c\,\mathrm{KL}(\pi\|b)\}
 =\Psi_{c,b}(v),
 \quad\text{with unique maximizer }q_{c,b}(v).                         \tag{14}
\]
For \(w=v+z\), the same substitution gives
\[
 c\,\mathrm{KL}\{q_{c,b}(w)\|b\}
 =w^\top q_{c,b}(w)-\Psi_{c,b}(w).                                    \tag{15}
\]
Take \(v=Ru_{n,j}\) and \(z=RE_{n,j}\).  The definitions of the oracle and
learned lotteries and (14)--(15) show, stratum by stratum, that the oracle
value of (13) minus its value at the learned lottery is
\[
 \Psi_{c,b_j}(v)-\Psi_{c,b_j}(v+z)+z^\top q_{c,b_j}(v+z)
 =\ell_{c,b_j}(v,z).                                                   \tag{16}
\]
Summing (16) with weights \(p_j\) proves
\[
 \sqrt n\,\mathscr R_n(c)
 =\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}p_j\ell_{c,b_j}(Ru_{n,j},RE_{n,j}).
\]
Multiplication by \(1+c\), the definition \(t=c/(1+c)\), and
\(\mathrm{def:compactified\mbox{-}path}\) give
\[
 (1+c)\sqrt n\,\mathscr R_n(c)=G(u_n,E_n)(t)=T_n(t).
\]
Consistency and randomization identify every \(\mu_{n,ja}\), and hence
the causal welfare functional used on the left; equation (16), rather than
a definition, proves its equality to the statistical path.  The values at
\(t=0\) and \(t=1\) are the limits proved in
\(\mathrm{lem:hard\mbox{-}endpoint}\) and
\(\mathrm{lem:high\mbox{-}endpoint}\).

For \(v\in\mathbb R^K\), differentiate \(q_{c,b}(sv)\) in \(s\):
\[
 {d\over ds}q_{c,b}(sv)={1\over c}C\{q_{c,b}(sv)\}v.
\]
For any probability vector \(r\),
\(\|C(r)v\|_1=\sum_ar_a|v_a-r^\top v|\le2\|v\|_\infty\).
Integration from zero to one therefore gives
\[
 \|q_{c,b}(v)-b\|_1\le{2\|v\|_\infty\over c}.                          \tag{17}
\]
For probability vectors \(r,b\), direct expansion of the two variances gives
\[
 |z^\top\{C(r)-C(b)\}z|
 \le3\|z\|_\infty^2\|r-b\|_1.                                        \tag{18}
\]
Multiplying the integral identity of
\(\mathrm{lem:bregman\mbox{-}identity}\) by \(c\), and then using
(17)--(18) with \(v=u+sz\), yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \left|c\ell_{c,b}(u,z)-{1\over2}z^\top C(b)z\right|
 &\le\int_0^1 3s\|z\|_\infty^2
       \|q_{c,b}(u+sz)-b\|_1\,ds\\
 &\le {3\|z\|_\infty^2(\|u\|_\infty+\|z\|_\infty)\over c}.
 \end{aligned}                                                        \tag{19}
\]
The last constant uses
\(\int_0^1 6s(\|u\|_\infty+s\|z\|_\infty)\,ds
\le3(\|u\|_\infty+\|z\|_\infty)\).

For \(x\in\mathbb R^{K-1}\), the pairwise variance identity and
\(Rx=(0,x_1,\ldots,x_{K-1})^\top\) give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 x^\top R^\top C(b)Rx
 &=\sum_{0\le a<r\le K-1}b_ab_r\{(Rx)_a-(Rx)_r\}^2\\
 &\ge b_0\sum_{r=1}^{K-1}b_rx_r^2
 \ge\beta^2\|x\|_2^2,                                                 
 \end{aligned}                                                        \tag{20}
\]
where the last line uses
\(\mathrm{ass:benchmark\mbox{-}support}\).
Since \((1+c)\ell=(1+c^{-1})c\ell\), (19) and the bound
\(|z^\top C(b)z|\le\|z\|_\infty^2\) give an explicit error of order
\[
 {\,\|z\|_\infty^2\{1+\|u\|_\infty+\|z\|_\infty\}\over c}
\]
between the interior coordinate and the quadratic endpoint.  Summing over
the finitely many strata proves the asserted locally uniform convergence as
\(t\uparrow1\).

Let \(M=\max_av_a\), \(I=I(v)\), and \(B_I=\sum_{a\in I}b_a\).
Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:benchmark\mbox{-}support}\) gives \(B_I\ge\beta\).
Factoring \(e^{M/c}\) out of the partition function gives
\[
 M+c\log B_I\le\Psi_{c,b}(v)\le M,
\qquad
 |\Psi_{c,b}(v)-M|\le c\log(1/\beta).                                 \tag{21}
\]
Conditional on \(I\), the Gibbs probabilities have exactly the proportions
\(b_a/B_I\).  The total Gibbs mass outside \(I\) is at most
\[
 {e^{-\gamma(v)/c}\sum_{a\notin I}b_a\over B_I}
 \le\beta^{-1}e^{-\gamma(v)/c}.
\]
Moving this mass from outside \(I\) to its benchmark proportions inside
\(I\) changes total variation by precisely that mass.  Hence
\[
 \|q_{c,b}(v)-q_{0,b}(v)\|_1
 \le2\beta^{-1}e^{-\gamma(v)/c}.                                      \tag{22}
\]
When every coordinate ties, both maps equal \(b\), and (22) remains true
under the convention \(\gamma(v)=\infty\).

For \(v=u+z\), the hard loss can equivalently be written
\[
 \ell_{0,b}(u,z)
 =\max_a u_a-\max_a v_a+z^\top q_{0,b}(v).
\]
Apply (21) at \(u\) and \(v\), and (22) at \(v\), to obtain
\[
 |\ell_{c,b}(u,z)-\ell_{0,b}(u,z)|
 \le2c\log(1/\beta)
 +2\|z\|_\infty\beta^{-1}e^{-\gamma(u+z)/c}.                           \tag{23}
\]

For the probability claim, fix a stratum and an unordered pair \(a<r\).
The difference of the corresponding coordinates of \(R(h_j+Z_{V,j})\)
is a nondegenerate univariate Gaussian.  Its contrast vector has Euclidean
norm at least one, so
\(\mathrm{ass:covariance\mbox{-}envelope}\) makes its variance at least
\(v_{\min}\).  A Gaussian density of variance at least \(v_{\min}\) is
bounded by \((2\pi v_{\min})^{-1/2}\), and therefore
\[
 P\!\left(\left|
 (R(h_j+Z_{V,j}))_a-(R(h_j+Z_{V,j}))_r
 \right|\le a_0\right)
 \le {2a_0\over\sqrt{2\pi v_{\min}}}.                                 \tag{24}
\]
There are \(JK(K-1)/2\) such pairs.  The union bound applied to (24) is
exactly
\[
 {JK(K-1)a_0\over\sqrt{2\pi v_{\min}}}.
\]
It charges every multiway tie through at least one of its constituent
pairs and is uniform in \(h\) and \(V\).

For \(0<t<1\), the defining formula for \(G(u,z)(t)\) is continuous in
\(t\).  Equation (23) proves continuity at \(t=0\), including an exact
multiway tie because the benchmark proportions on the maximizing set agree
for every \(c>0\).  Equation (19) proves continuity at \(t=1\).  Thus
\(G(u,z)\in C([0,1])\) for every \(u,z\).

The two global bounds in \(\mathrm{lem:bregman\mbox{-}identity}\) imply,
for \(B=\|z\|_\infty\),
\[
 0\le G(u,z)(t)
 \le\sum_jp_j\left\{\operatorname{osc}(Rz_j)
       +{\operatorname{osc}(Rz_j)^2\over8}\right\}
 \le2B+{B^2\over2}.                                                    \tag{25}
\]
The endpoint formulas satisfy the same bound by passage to the limit.
Consequently \(S(h,Z_V)\) is finite almost surely, indeed for every finite
realization of \(Z_V\).

The hard maximizing sets are determined by finitely many weak coordinate
inequalities, so \(q_{0,b}\) is Borel.  All interior coordinate evaluations
are continuous and the two endpoint evaluations are Borel.  Since
\(C([0,1])\) is separable and its Borel sigma-field is generated by
evaluations at rational times, \((u,z)\mapsto G(u,z)\) is Borel into
\(C([0,1])\).

Now let \(h_m\to h\) and \(V_m\to V\) within the two compact parameter
sets, and use the common-normal realization
\[
 Z_{V_m}=V_m^{1/2}Z,\qquad Z_V=V^{1/2}Z,\qquad Z\sim N(0,I_d).           \tag{26}
\]
Continuity of the positive-definite square-root gives
\(Z_{V_m}\to Z_V\) almost surely.  By (24), with \(a_0\downarrow0\),
the probability that \(R(h_j+Z_{V,j})\) has any tie is zero.  Off this
null set the winning profile is locally constant.  Equation (23) controls
a common neighborhood of \(t=0\), equation (19) controls one of \(t=1\),
and ordinary smoothness controls the remaining compact temperature interval.
It follows that
\[
 \|G(h_m,Z_{V_m})-G(h,Z_V)\|_\infty\longrightarrow0
\quad\text{almost surely}.                                            \tag{27}
\]
The supremum map is one-Lipschitz, so (27) proves weak continuity of the
law of \(S(h,Z_V)\) at every continuity set.

Finally (25), the Gaussian union bound, and
\(\lambda_{\max}(V)\le v_{\max}\) give
\[
 \sup_{h,V}P\{S(h,Z_V)>2B+B^2/2\}
 \le2d\exp\{-B^2/(2v_{\max})\}\longrightarrow0.                        \tag{28}
\]
Thus the defining set for \(Q_{1-\alpha}^{\mathrm{LF}}\) is nonempty and
the quantile is finite.  If \(q_m\downarrow Q_{1-\alpha}^{\mathrm{LF}}\)
with every \(q_m\) in that defining set, continuity from above of each
CDF gives
\[
 \inf_{h,V}P\{S(h,Z_V)\le Q_{1-\alpha}^{\mathrm{LF}}\}\ge1-\alpha.
\]
This is the claimed right-quantile coverage statement and does not require
absence of atoms.

Every cell count and cell sum in \(\widehat\mu_{n,ja}\) is
\(\mathcal F_n^{\mathrm{obs}}\)-measurable.  The empty-cell convention is
deterministic, so \(\widehat\Delta_n\), \(\widehat u_n\), and
\(\widehat p_n\) are measurable with respect to that sigma-field.  For fixed
finite \(c>0\), the exponential and logarithm formulas defining the plug-in
frontier are continuous functions of these finitely many statistics.  The
hard endpoint is Borel because it is formed from finitely many maxima, and
the quadratic endpoint is continuous.  The endpoint estimates (19) and
(23), applied with \(\widehat u_n\), show that each realized plug-in path is
continuous.  Separability of \(C([0,1])\) then shows that
\(\widehat{\mathfrak F}_n\) is a
\(\mathcal F_n^{\mathrm{obs}}\)-measurable random element.  Its displayed
formula uses only the observed triples, the supplied benchmark \(b\), and
the declared cell estimators; in particular it nowhere uses
\(\Delta_n,u_n\), or \(E_n\).

For every function \(f\in C([0,1])\), every \(s\in[0,1]\), and every real
\(x\), the deterministic implication
\[
 \sup_{t\in[0,1]}f(t)\le x\quad\Longrightarrow\quad f(s)\le x           \tag{29}
\]
holds.  Apply (29) pointwise with \(f=T_n\) and
\(s=\widehat t_n\).  Measurability of the selector is needed only to make
the right-hand event measurable; no independence is used.  This proves
\[
 \{\sup_tT_n(t)\le x\}\subseteq\{T_n(\widehat t_n)\le x\}.              \tag{30}
\]
On \(0<\widehat t_n<1\), put
\(\widehat c_n=\widehat t_n/(1-\widehat t_n)\).  The exact identity in
\(\mathrm{lem:exact\mbox{-}regret\mbox{-}path}\), evaluated at the
realized positive value \(\widehat c_n\), gives
\[
 T_n(\widehat t_n)
 =(1+\widehat c_n)\sqrt n\,\mathscr R_n(\widehat c_n).                 \tag{31}
\]
Equations (30)--(31) prove the bridge and also show why no equality between
the observable frontier and the oracle regret path is required.

Write
\[
 H_0=\sup_{h\in\mathcal H}\|h\|_\infty<\infty,\qquad
 x_n=\sqrt{r_n}+\rho_n .
\]
We first turn the bounded-Lipschitz bound into a coupling without imposing
any new assumption.  For a closed set \(A\) and \(\delta\in(0,1]\), the
ramp \(x\mapsto(1-\operatorname{dist}(x,A)/\delta)_+\) is bounded by one
and has Lipschitz constant \(\delta^{-1}\).  Therefore
\[
 P(E_n\in A)\le P(Z_{V_n}\in A^\delta)+r_n/\delta .
\]
With \(\delta=\sqrt{r_n}\), the same inequality with the two laws
interchanged gives the defining inequalities for Prokhorov distance
\(\sqrt{r_n}\).  Approximating both laws by finite rational partitions and
applying the finite marriage lemma, then taking a tight subsequential limit,
constructs a coupling satisfying
\[
 P\{\|E_n-Z_{V_n}\|_\infty>\sqrt{r_n}\}\le\sqrt{r_n}.                  \tag{32}
\]
This construction is the elementary proof of the coupling implication; it
does not add an assumption to the model.

Fix \(M\ge1\) and \(0<a\le1/4\) with \(x_n\le a/8\).  Let
\(\mathcal B(M,a)\) be the event on which (32) succeeds,
\(\|Z_{V_n}\|_\infty\le M\), and every within-stratum pairwise coordinate
gap of \(R(h+Z_{V_n})\) exceeds \(a\).  The Gaussian coordinate tail bound
and (24) give
\[
 P\{\mathcal B(M,a)^c\}
 \le\sqrt{r_n}
 +2d e^{-M^2/(2v_{\max})}
 +{JK(K-1)a\over\sqrt{2\pi v_{\min}}}.                               \tag{33}
\]
On this event,
\[
 \|u_n-h\|_\infty\le\rho_n,\qquad
 \|E_n-Z_{V_n}\|_\infty\le\sqrt{r_n},
\]
so every hard winning action is unchanged when
\((h,Z_{V_n})\) is replaced by \((u_n,E_n)\).

For completeness, we derive the deterministic path modulus used on
\(\mathcal B(M,a)\).  Put
\[
 c_0={a\over8\log\{\exp(1)+M/a\}}.
\]
For \(0<c\le c_0\), apply (23) to both paths.  Their common hard profile,
the two-Lipschitz dependence of the hard loss on its first argument, and
\(\exp(-a/(2c))\le\{a/(\exp(1)+M/a)\}^4\) yield
\[
 \sup_{0<c\le c_0}
 |(1+c)L_c(u_n,E_n)-(1+c)L_c(h,Z_{V_n})|
 \le C_0\{Ma+x_n\},                                                   \tag{34}
\]
where \(L_c(u,z)=\sum_jp_j\ell_{c,b_j}(Ru_j,Rz_j)\) and
\[
 C_0=2^8JK^2\beta^{-2}(1+H_0).
\]
For \(c\ge c_0\), differentiate the integral representation (11) in both
arguments.  The identities
\[
 Dq_{c,b}(v)={1\over c}C\{q_{c,b}(v)\},\qquad
 \|C(r)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le1,
\]
together with (17)--(18), give, along the segment joining the two input
pairs,
\[
 \sup_{c\ge c_0}
 |(1+c)L_c(u_n,E_n)-(1+c)L_c(h,Z_{V_n})|
 \le C_1\,{x_n(1+M)^2
 \log\{\exp(1)+M/a\}\over a},                                        \tag{35}
\]
where one admissible explicit value is
\[
 C_1=2^{10}JK^2\beta^{-2}(1+H_0)(1+v_{\max}+v_{\min}^{-1}).
\]
For \(c\ge1/c_0\), the apparent factor \(c\) in this differentiation is
cancelled by subtracting the quadratic endpoint and using (19); this is why
the right side of (35), rather than a bound growing with \(c\), holds.
The same calculations at \(c=0\) and \(c=\infty\) prove that (34)--(35)
include both compactified endpoints.  Combining them and enlarging the
constant gives
\[
 \|G(u_n,E_n)-G(h,Z_{V_n})\|_\infty
 \le C_2\left[
 Ma+{x_n(1+M)^2\log\{\exp(1)+M/a\}\over a}\right]                     \tag{36}
\]
on \(\mathcal B(M,a)\), with
\[
 C_2=2^{12}JK^2\beta^{-2}p_{\min}^{-1}
 (1+H_0)^2(1+v_{\max}+v_{\min}^{-1}).
\]

Let \(F\) be bounded by one and one-Lipschitz for the bounded supremum norm
on \(C([0,1])\).  On \(\mathcal B(M,a)\), use (36); on its complement use
\(|F|\le1\).  Equations (33)--(36) imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\left|E F\{G(u_n,E_n)\}-E F\{G(h,Z_{V_n})\}\right|\\
 &\quad\le C_{\mathrm{map}}\left[
 \sqrt{r_n}+{JK^2a\over\sqrt{v_{\min}}}
 +d e^{-M^2/(2v_{\max})}+Ma
 +{x_n(1+M)^2\log\{\exp(1)+M/a\}\over a}\right],                      \tag{37}
 \end{aligned}
\]
where the explicit computable choice
\[
 C_{\mathrm{map}}
 =2^{14}JK^2\beta^{-2}p_{\min}^{-1}
 (1+H_0)^2(1+v_{\max}+v_{\min}^{-1})
\]
dominates every numerical constant above.  Taking the displayed infimum in
\(\mathrm{def:curve\mbox{-}rate}\) proves the asserted uniform
bounded-Lipschitz inequality.

It remains to check the limit.  Because \(r_n=C_{\mathrm{BE}}n^{-1/2}\)
and \(\rho_n\downarrow0\), \(x_n\downarrow0\).  For example, set
\[
 a_n=x_n^{1/3},\qquad
 M_n=\max\{1,\sqrt{2v_{\max}\log(1/x_n)}\}.
\]
For all sufficiently large \(n\), the constraint \(x_n\le a_n/8\) holds.
Every term in the bracket in (37) then tends to zero; the last is
\(O\{x_n^{2/3}\log^2(1/x_n)\}\).  Hence \(\varepsilon_n\to0\).
Finally, (32) is a coupling of \(E_n\) and \(Z_{V_n}\) itself, and all
path comparisons were made on that same probability space.  Thus (37)
also holds for the joint pairs
\((T_n,E_n)\) and \((G(h,Z_{V_n}),Z_{V_n})\) under the corresponding
bounded product norm, which proves the asserted joint version.

Let
\[
 \delta_n=\alpha-\sqrt{\overline\varepsilon_n}-\gamma>0.
\]
Every oracle in \(\mathfrak R\) is total by
\(\mathrm{def:effective\mbox{-}input}\).  Binary range reduction and the
alternating Taylor formulas for \(\exp\) and \(\log\), with the first
omitted term rounded outward, return rational enclosing intervals of width
at most \(2^{-m}\) after finitely many rational operations.  Symmetric
Gaussian elimination with outward interval pivots likewise verifies a
strict spectral exclusion; an undecided covariance box is retained, so no
law in \(\mathcal K_V\) can be lost.

The algorithm has an initialization node and at most \(w_{\max}\)
subdivision nodes.  At each node it enumerates the \(K^J\) hard profiles.
The interval evaluation ledger uses at most
\[
 K^J\{8+4d+d(d+1)\}
\]
box primitives per node.  Range reduction for the coordinate tail bound
uses at most \(4d(m_{\mathsf A}+1)\) further oracle primitives.  Adding the
initial operation gives exactly the declared upper bound
\[
 N_{\mathsf A}
 =1+(w_{\max}+1)K^J\{8+4d+d(d+1)\}
   +4d(m_{\mathsf A}+1).                                               \tag{38}
\]
Every requested precision is at most \(m_{\mathsf A}\) by construction.
Thus either a refined certificate is accepted within this finite loop or
the fallback is emitted, and the algorithm halts.

We next prove the semantic implication checked by the certificate.  On the
refined branch, outward inclusion of every path interval implies
\[
 \sup_{t\in[0,1]}G(h,z)(t)
 \le \max_{\tau\in\mathcal P_t}G(h',z')(\tau)
    +\omega_t+\omega_h+\omega_V
\]
for some covering grid representatives \(h',V',z'\).  The lower Gaussian
box sums use density lower intervals, while discarded tail, integration,
and floating-point contributions are subtracted.  Consequently the exact
rational checks defining \(L_{\mathrm{CDF}}\) imply
\[
 \inf_{h\in\mathcal H,V\in\mathcal K_V}
 P\{S(h,Z_V)\le Q^+_{n,\alpha}
       +\omega_t+\omega_h+\omega_V\}
 \ge1-\alpha+\sqrt{\overline\varepsilon_n}.                           \tag{39}
\]
The checked inequality
\(\omega_t+\omega_h+\omega_V\le\zeta\) turns (39) into the conclusion of
the theorem.  Notice that only a lower CDF sum is inverted; no continuity
of that CDF is used.

For the fallback branch, (25) gives, on
\(\|Z_V\|_\infty\le B_\gamma^+\),
\[
 S(h,Z_V)\le2B_\gamma^++{(B_\gamma^+)^2\over2}
 =Q^+_{n,\alpha}.                                                      \tag{40}
\]
For each coordinate, \(\operatorname{Var}(Z_{V,k})\le v_{\max}\), so the
union Gaussian-tail bound and the rational inequality checked by the
certificate give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \sup_{V\in\mathcal K_V}
 P(\|Z_V\|_\infty>B_\gamma^+)
 &\le2d\exp\{-(B_\gamma^+)^2/(2v_{\max})\}\\
 &\le\alpha-\sqrt{\overline\varepsilon_n}-\gamma.                     \tag{41}
 \end{aligned}
\]
Equations (40)--(41) are stronger than the required lower probability,
even before adding \(\zeta\).  They also show directly why an atom at the
fallback value causes no error.

The formula defining \(m_{\mathsf A}\) supplies enough range-reduction
bits for the rational padding in (40)--(41), and \(B_\gamma^+\) is rounded
upward; hence the fallback certificate always closes.  Finally, exact
rational addition and multiplication increase numerator and denominator
bit lengths by at most an additive amount per operation, while the
range-reduced Taylor algorithms use a number of arithmetic steps polynomial
in their input and output lengths.  Under the stipulated unit cost for each
interval primitive, the total bit cost is therefore polynomial in
\(N_{\mathsf A}\), the maximum input bit length, and the oracle-output bit
length at \(m_{\mathsf A}\).  This completes the termination, verification,
and complexity claims.

Put \(\delta_n=\sqrt{\overline\varepsilon_n}\) and
\(q_n=Q^+_{n,\alpha}+\zeta\).  The calibration theorem gives
\[
 \inf_{h\in\mathcal H,V\in\mathcal K_V}
 P\{S(h,Z_V)\le q_n\}\ge1-\alpha+\delta_n.                             \tag{42}
\]
Define the one-sided ramp
\[
 \varphi_n(x)=
 \begin{cases}
 1,&x\le q_n,\\
 1-(x-q_n)/\delta_n,&q_n<x<q_n+\delta_n,\\
 0,&x\ge q_n+\delta_n.
 \end{cases}
\]
It is bounded by one and has Lipschitz constant \(\delta_n^{-1}\).
Because the supremum is one-Lipschitz on \(C([0,1])\), the
bounded-Lipschitz inequality in
\(\mathrm{thm:uniform\mbox{-}path\mbox{-}law}\) implies, uniformly in the
row law,
\[
 \left|E_{P_n}\varphi_n\{\sup_tT_n(t)\}
 -E\varphi_n\{S(h,Z_{V_n})\}\right|
 \le {\varepsilon_n\over\delta_n}\le\delta_n.                          \tag{43}
\]
Here the bounded version of the norm permits the same conclusion when
\(\delta_n\le1\), which holds eventually; the finitely many earlier rows
do not affect the limit inferior.  Since
\({\bf1}\{x\le q_n\}\le\varphi_n(x)\le
{\bf1}\{x\le q_n+\delta_n\}\), (42)--(43) give, for every sufficiently
large \(n\),
\[
 \inf_{(P_n)\in\mathcal M}
 P_n\{\sup_{t\in[0,1]}T_n(t)\le
 Q^+_{n,\alpha}+\zeta+\sqrt{\overline\varepsilon_n}\}
 \ge1-\alpha.                                                         \tag{44}
\]
The threshold in (44) is \(C_{n,\alpha}\).  Taking the uniform limit
inferior proves simultaneous coverage.

For every observed-data measurable selector, the deterministic inclusion
(30) turns (44) into
\[
 \liminf_n\inf_{(P_n)\in\mathcal M}
 P_n\{T_n(\widehat t_n)\le C_{n,\alpha}\}\ge1-\alpha.                  \tag{45}
\]
At an interior choice, (31) identifies the event in (45) with
\[
 \{(1+\widehat c_n)\sqrt n\,\mathscr R_n(\widehat c_n)
       \le C_{n,\alpha}\}.
\]
The selector may be any Borel functional of the observable plug-in frontier
by \(\mathrm{lem:operational\mbox{-}selector\mbox{-}bridge}\).
Crucially, (42) uses a verified lower CDF and the ramp decreases only to
the right.  Thus every atom at \(q_n\) is included in (42), and neither
(43) nor (44) invokes an anti-concentration or quantile-continuity
condition.

In the stated binary submodel write \(z\) for the single contrast and
\[
 L(s)={e^s\over1+e^s}.
\]
For \(u=0\), direct differentiation of the Bregman formula gives, for
\(z>0\) and every \(c>0\),
\[
 {d\over dz}\ell_{c,b}(0,(0,z))
 ={z\over c}L(z/c)\{1-L(z/c)\}>0.                                    \tag{46}
\]
The uniform benchmark makes the loss even in \(z\), by interchanging the
two action labels and using translation invariance of \(\Psi\).  Its
quadratic endpoint is \(z^2/8\), and the hard endpoint is zero.  Hence
\[
 s_0(r):=S(0,r)
\]
is even and strictly increasing for \(r>0\).  To justify strictness for
the supremum, note that the quadratic endpoint is positive for \(r>0\),
whereas the finite-\(c\) expression tends to zero as \(c\downarrow0\).
Thus, on any compact interval \(0<r_-\le r\le r_+\), every maximizing or
asymptotically maximizing temperature lies in a compact subset of
\((0,\infty]\).  Equation (46), together with derivative \(r/4\) at
\(c=\infty\), then supplies constants \(0<m<M<\infty\) such that
\[
 m(r_2-r_1)\le s_0(r_2)-s_0(r_1)\le M(r_2-r_1)                        \tag{47}
\]
whenever \(r_1<r_2\) are sufficiently close in that compact interval.

Let \(a_\alpha=\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)>0\).  Since
\(|Z_V|=\sqrt V\,|Z_1|\) and \(s_0\) is strictly increasing, its right
\((1-\alpha)\)-quantile is
\[
 q_{1-\alpha}(V)=s_0(a_\alpha\sqrt V).                                \tag{48}
\]
Fix the asserted interior \(V\).  For all sufficiently small \(s>0\),
both arguments in (48) lie in one compact interval away from zero, and
\[
 {a_\alpha s\over2\sqrt V}
 \le a_\alpha\{\sqrt V-\sqrt{V-s}\}
 ={a_\alpha s\over\sqrt V+\sqrt{V-s}}
 \le {a_\alpha s\over2\sqrt{V-s}}.                                   \tag{49}
\]
Combining (47)--(49) gives constants \(c_1,c_2,s_0>0\) for which
\[
 c_1s\le q_{1-\alpha}(V)-q_{1-\alpha}(V-s)\le c_2s
\quad(0<s<s_0).
\]
If a localized calibration can replace \(V\) by \(V-s\), an inflation
smaller than the left side fails at the right quantile in (48).  The lower
bound therefore rules out uniformly honest \(o(s)\) inflation, while the
upper bound establishes order sharpness.

theorem.statement:
For fixed \(h\in\mathcal H\) and \(V\in\mathcal K_V\), every atom of
\(S(h,Z_V)\) is a flat hard-profile atom.  More precisely, for
\(\mathbf a=(a_1,\ldots,a_J)\in\mathcal A^J\), define
\[
 L_{\mathbf a}(h)=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}p_j
 \left[\max_{r\in\mathcal A}(Rh_j)_r-(Rh_j)_{a_j}\right],
 \quad
 \mathcal D_{\mathbf a}(h)=
 \left\{z:(R(h_j+z_j))_{a_j}>
 (R(h_j+z_j))_r\ \text{for all }r\ne a_j,\ j\in\mathcal J\right\},
\]
and \(U_h(z)=\sup_{0<t\le1}G(h,z)(t)\).  Then the atom at \(q\) has mass
\[
 \sum_{\mathbf a:L_{\mathbf a}(h)=q}
 P\{Z_V\in\mathcal D_{\mathbf a}(h),\
 U_h(Z_V)\le L_{\mathbf a}(h)\}.
\]
Thus the finite list \(\{L_{\mathbf a}(h):\mathbf a\in\mathcal A^J\}\)
and the displayed Gaussian plateau integrals characterize all atoms.
Nevertheless, under the frozen assumptions alone there is no computable
modulus \(A(x)\downarrow0\) that bounds
\(P\{q<S(h,Z_V)\le q+x\}\) uniformly in \(h,V,q\) after deleting only
the atom at \(q\): a legal two-stratum binary submodel has two positive-mass
hard-profile atoms whose locations coalesce while both masses stay bounded
away from zero.  Consequently a prescribed two-sided value-width bracket
for \(Q_{1-\alpha}^{\mathrm{LF}}\) is not certified without an additional
uniform separation or no-plateau condition.  The one-sided algorithm
\(\mathsf A\) remains valid.
theorem.proof_tex:
Fix \(h,V\), and abbreviate
\[
 U_h(z)=\sup_{0<t\le1}G(h,z)(t).
\]
The pairwise Gaussian calculation (24) shows that, with probability one,
every \(R(h_j+Z_{V,j})\) has a unique maximizing coordinate.  Off this
null boundary the hard endpoint is constant on the polyhedral cell
\(\mathcal D_{\mathbf a}(h)\), with value \(L_{\mathbf a}(h)\), and
\[
 S(h,z)=\max\{L_{\mathbf a}(h),U_h(z)\}
 \quad\text{on }\mathcal D_{\mathbf a}(h).                             \tag{50}
\]

We show that \(U_h\) cannot create any other atom.  Fix a nonzero direction
\(\omega\) and write \(z=r\omega\), \(r>0\).  For every \(c>0\),
differentiation of (11) in \(r\) gives
\[
 {d\over dr}\ell_{c,b}(Ru,R(r\omega))
 ={r\over c}(R\omega)^\top
 C\{q_{c,b}(R(u+r\omega))\}R\omega.                                   \tag{51}
\]
All coordinates of \(q_{c,b}\) are positive.  Therefore the sum over
strata in (51) is strictly positive whenever \(\omega\ne0\); the projected
positive-definiteness (20) gives the same conclusion at \(c=\infty\).
It follows that \(r\mapsto U_h(r\omega)\) is nondecreasing.

Suppose it is constant on a nondegenerate radial interval.  A sequence of
temperatures approaching the supremum at the left endpoint cannot remain
in a compact subset of \((0,\infty]\), because (51) would then give a
strict, locally uniform increase.  It must therefore tend to zero.
Equation (23) shows that the common value is the hard-profile value on
that radial interval.  Hence, for any
\(q\notin\{L_{\mathbf a}(h):\mathbf a\in\mathcal A^J\}\), every radial
section of \(\{z:U_h(z)=q\}\) contains at most one point.  Polar-coordinate
Fubini then gives this level set Lebesgue measure zero.  Since \(Z_V\) has
a strictly positive Lebesgue density, it has Gaussian probability zero.
Combining this fact with (50) proves both that every atom is in the stated
finite list and that its mass is exactly
\[
 \sum_{\mathbf a:L_{\mathbf a}(h)=q}
 P\{Z_V\in\mathcal D_{\mathbf a}(h),\
 U_h(Z_V)\le L_{\mathbf a}(h)\}.                                     \tag{52}
\]
The list is finite and directly computable; each mass in (52) is a
one-sided Gaussian integral over an explicitly given plateau set.

It remains to test uniform small intervals.  We construct a legal collision.
Take \(J=2\), \(K=2\), \(p_1=p_2=1/2\), \(V=I_2\), and in both strata use
the positive benchmark \(b=(b_0,b_1)=(1-\eta,\eta)\), where \(\eta>0\)
will be a sufficiently small rational number.  Let
\[
 L_b(s)={b_1e^s\over b_0+b_1e^s}.
\]
For a positive true binary contrast \(r\) and an error \(z<-r\), the
estimated hard action is zero and the hard loss is \(r\).  Direct
substitution, or (10), shows that its finite-temperature normalized loss
\(F_{\eta,r,z}(c)=(1+c)\ell_{c,b}((0,r),(0,z))\) extends continuously to
\([0,\infty]\), with
\[
 F_{\eta,r,z}(0)=r,\qquad
 F_{\eta,r,z}(\infty)={b_0b_1z^2\over2}.                              \tag{53}
\]
The unique true and estimated maximizers are different, so the
log-sum-exp formula also gives the right derivative
\[
 \lim_{c\downarrow0}
 {F_{\eta,r,z}(c)-r\over c}
 =r+\log{b_1\over b_0}.                                                \tag{54}
\]
For clarity, (54) follows by writing the two Gibbs probabilities as
\(L_b(r/c)\) and \(L_b((r+z)/c)\); the exponentially small remainders obey
\[
 \lim_{s\downarrow0}{L_b(s)-b_1\over s}=b_0b_1,
 \qquad
 \lim_{s\downarrow0}
 {sL_b(s)-\log(b_0+b_1e^s)\over s^2}
 ={b_0b_1\over2}.                                                      \tag{55}
\]
All backslashes in (55) are literal TeX commands.

Choose a rational \(r_*>0\) and a compact interval
\(r\in[r_*,2r_*]\), and choose \(z\) in a compact interval strictly below
\(-2r_*\).  First take \(\eta\) so small that
\[
 2r_*+\log\{\eta/(1-\eta)\}<-1
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \eta(1-\eta)\sup z^2/2<r_*/4.                                       \tag{56}
\]
Equations (53)--(54) make \(F_{\eta,r,z}(c)<r\) uniformly for all
sufficiently small \(c>0\).  On every interval \(c\ge c_0>0\), the exact
Gibbs formula converges uniformly to zero as \(\eta\downarrow0\), including
\(c=\infty\) by (53).  Decreasing the rational \(\eta\) once more therefore
gives
\[
 F_{\eta,r,z}(c)<r\qquad\text{for every }c>0                           \tag{57}
\]
uniformly on smaller nonempty intervals of \(r\) and \(z\).

In the other stratum take the error in a sufficiently small neighborhood
of zero, so its learned hard action is the correct action.  Its normalized
loss is zero at error zero and is uniformly continuous on the compactified
temperature interval by (19) and (23).  The strict margins in
(56)--(57) therefore give an open rectangle of two-dimensional errors on
which the first stratum is wrong, the second is correct, and the total
supremum equals the hard value \(r_1/2\).  Interchanging the strata gives
another open rectangle on which it equals \(r_2/2\).  The rectangles and
the inequalities may be chosen uniformly for
\[
 r_1=r_*,\qquad r_2=r_*+2\delta,\qquad0<\delta<\delta_0.
\]
Because the \(N(0,I_2)\) density is positive, both rectangles have
probability at least a constant \(m_0>0\), independent of \(\delta\).
Choose a rational hyperrectangle \(\mathcal H\) containing these contrasts,
take \(v_{\min}<1<v_{\max}\), and set \(\beta=\eta\); all frozen support,
compactness, and covariance conditions are then satisfied.

Thus \(S(h_\delta,Z_V)\) has atoms of mass at least \(m_0\) at
\[
 q_\delta={r_*\over2},
 \qquad q_\delta+\delta={r_*+2\delta\over2}.
\]
For \(x_\delta=2\delta\),
\[
 P\{q_\delta<S(h_\delta,Z_V)\le q_\delta+x_\delta\}\ge m_0.            \tag{58}
\]
The open lower endpoint in (58) removes the atom at \(q_\delta\), yet
\(x_\delta\downarrow0\).  Hence no uniform \(A(x)\downarrow0\) of the
requested kind can follow from the frozen assumptions.  A two-sided
quantile-width guarantee would need, for example, a uniform positive
separation between distinct positive-mass values in (52), or a condition
making every plateau integral there zero.  The one-sided lower-CDF
certificate proved in \(\mathrm{thm:certified\mbox{-}calibration}\) uses
neither condition and therefore remains valid.
